clues.text: I was Simon Peter's brother.
I immediately abandoned my nets and followed Jesus.
I was a fisherman.
I was one of the twelve apostles.
Jesus called me to become a fisher of men.
My city was Bethsaida.
After Jesus' ascension I was in an upper room with the other apostles.
I heard John say, “See, the Lamb of God!” and followed Jesus.
I told Simon, “We have found the Messiah.”
I was casting a net into the sea of Galilee when Jesus called me.
I was first a disciple of John.
Jesus entered the house of Simon and me.
I said the loaves would not go far among so many.
I stayed with Jesus that day after asking where he was staying.
I told Jesus there was a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish.
On the Mount of Olives I asked Jesus privately about the sign, with Peter, James, and John.
From Bethsaida fishing I became one of four who asked Jesus for the sign opposite the temple.
Leaving John after he said, “See, the Lamb of God!” I first found my own brother Simon.
When Philip told me Greeks wanted to see Jesus, he and I went and told Jesus.
I was a prophetess.
I was the daughter of Phanuel.
I was of the tribe of Asher.
I was a widow.
I was never missing from the temple.
I lived with a husband for seven years from my virginity.
I was a widow until 84 years.
I rendered sacred service night and day.
I came near at that very hour when the child was at the temple.
I spoke about the child to all who were waiting for Jerusalem's deliverance.
After seven years of marriage, I remained a widow into old age and was never missing from the temple.
Night and day at the temple I used fastings and supplications.
I was an Asherite prophetess, widow to 84, never missing from the temple.
At the child's presentation I thanked God and spoke to those waiting for Jerusalem's deliverance.
From Phanuel's line in Asher I served in the temple until I bore witness about the child.
I was father-in-law of Caiaphas.
Jesus was led to me first after his arrest.
I was called a chief priest.
I sent Jesus away bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
During John's ministry the word of God came in the days of my high priesthood with Caiaphas.
I questioned Jesus about his disciples.
I questioned Jesus about his teaching.
Jesus told me he had spoken publicly in synagogue and temple.
Jesus told me to question those who heard him.
An officer slapped Jesus for the way he answered me.
I was present when Peter and John were examined.
After Jesus answered me, I sent him bound to Caiaphas.
I was listed with Caiaphas, John, and Alexander among the rulers.
With relatives of the chief priest I faced the apostles over a healed man.
Jesus came to me first because I was Caiaphas's father-in-law, then I sent him bound to Caiaphas.
I questioned Jesus about disciples and teaching, then an officer struck him for answering me.
I was named with Caiaphas when Peter and John were asked by what power the crippled man was healed.
I was a prisoner.
The crowd asked for me instead of Jesus.
Pilate released me.
I was a robber.
I was called a notorious prisoner.
I had been thrown into prison for sedition.
I had been thrown into prison for murder.
I was among the rebels who had committed murder in the sedition.
The chief priests stirred the crowd to choose me.
Pilate asked whether to release me or Jesus called Christ.
The whole crowd cried out together for me to be released.
The crowd demanded my release instead of Jesus.
Imprisoned for sedition and murder, I was released while Jesus was handed over.
The crowd chose me, a robber, over the King of the Jews.
For a festival release, they asked for me, a murderer, instead of Jesus.
I was one of the twelve apostles.
Philip found me and spoke to me about Jesus the son of Joseph from Nazareth..
I asked Philip "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?"
Jesus saw me under the fig tree.
I said to Jesus, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God.”
I was from Cana of Galilee.
Philip told me they had found the one Moses and the Prophets wrote about.
Philip told me, “Come and see.”
Jesus said I was truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.
I asked Jesus, “How do you know me?”
I said to Jesus, “You are King of Israel.”
Jesus asked if I believed because he saw me under the fig tree.
Jesus told me I would see things greater than his seeing me under the fig tree.
Jesus told us we would see heaven opened and angels ascending and descending to the Son of man.
In the apostle lists I was named with Philip.
Skeptical about Nazareth, I came and was named an Israelite with no deceit.
After Jesus died and was raised, I went fishing with Peter and others on the Sea of Tiberias.
From Cana I followed from that first call through to fishing again on Tiberias after his resurrection.
I was blind.
I was a beggar.
I was sitting beside the road near Jericho.
I called Jesus “Son of David.”
Jesus restored my sight.
I was the son of Timaeus.
I shouted, “Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked me, telling me to be silent.
All the more I kept shouting for mercy.
When Jesus called me, I threw off my outer garment.
I leaped to my feet and went to Jesus.
I said, “Rabboni, let me recover my sight.”
Jesus said to me, “Go. Your faith has made you well.”
Immediately I recovered my sight and began to follow Jesus on the road from Jericho.
After I could see, I followed him, glorifying God.
I asked what the crowd meant when Jesus was passing by.
Rebuked to silence at Jericho, I shouted louder until Jesus called me.
I threw aside my garment, asked for sight, and followed Jesus on the road from Jericho.
A blind beggar beside Jericho's road, I confessed him as Son of David and received my sight.
Annas was my father-in-law.
From my counsel they conspired to kill Jesus.
I said it was better for one man to die in behalf of the people.
I was high priest.
Jesus was led to me for trial.
Chief priests and older men gathered in my palace courtyard to plot against Jesus.
I asked what further need we had of witnesses.
I had advised that one man should die in behalf of the people.
I ripped my garments and said, “He has blasphemed!”
I said it was to their benefit that one man die rather than the whole nation be destroyed.
I said to Jesus, “I put you under oath by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God!”
I told the Sanhedrin they did not know anything at all.
I was high priest that year.
I was named with Annas when Peter and John were examined.
They led Jesus from me to the governor's residence.
False witnesses spoke against Jesus at my house.
I said Jesus had blasphemed and was liable to death.
Jesus said to me, “You yourself said it.”
We ordered the apostles not to teach on the basis of Jesus' name.
At the council, others warned that the Romans might take away our place and nation; I answered that one man should die for the people.
As high priest that year I prophesied—not of my own originality—that Jesus was to die for the nation.
I ripped my garments and said he had blasphemed, asking what further need we had of witnesses.
I was traveling to Emmaus.
I was going to Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
Jesus walked with me, but I did not recognize him at first.
I recognized Jesus when he broke the bread.
That same hour I returned to Jerusalem.
On the day Jesus was raised, I walked with another disciple to Emmaus.
We stood still, looking sad, when the stranger asked what we were debating.
I asked if he was a stranger in Jerusalem who did not know what had occurred.
I said Jesus the Nazarene proved to be a prophet powerful in deed and word.
I said our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death.
We had been hoping he was the one who was going to deliver Israel.
My companion and I said that it was the third day since Jesus was handed over to be sentenced to death.
I reported that women from among us astonished us at the tomb.
I said some of those with us found the tomb as the women said but did not see him.
He interpreted to us things about himself from Moses and all the Prophets.
We urged him, “Stay with us, because it is almost evening.”
My heart was burning as Jesus opened up the Scriptures on the road to Emmaus.
We related how he became known to us by the breaking of the bread.
Sad on the Emmaus road, I told the unrecognized Lord the story of the third day.
After urging him to stay, I knew him in the bread—and he disappeared.
From a burned heart on the road to Emmaus I rose that hour to tell the Eleven what happened.
I was the wife of Zechariah the priest.
I became mother to John.
I was from the daughters of Aaron.
I was barren.
My husband and I were well along in years.
Mary came to my home and greeted me.
At Mary's greeting, the infant in my womb leaped.
I insisted my son be called John.
Zechariah and I were both righteous before God.
We walked blamelessly in Jehovah's commandments and legal requirements.
An angel told Zechariah I would become mother to a son.
After I became pregnant, I kept myself secluded for five months.
I said Jehovah had looked on me to take away my reproach among men.
Gabriel told Mary I had conceived a son in my old age.
I was in my sixth month when Gabriel spoke to Mary.
I was filled with holy spirit when Mary greeted me.
I called Mary blessed among women.
I said the fruit of Mary's womb was blessed.
Neighbors and relatives rejoiced with me at my son's birth.
Relatives wanted to name my son Zechariah after his father.
Mary was my relative.
I asked how the privilege was mine to have the mother of my Lord come to me.
I said as soon as the sound of Mary's greeting fell on my ears, the infant leaped for joy.
I said happy is she who believed there would be a complete fulfillment of Jehovah's words.
People said none of my relatives was called John.
After I refused the name Zechariah, they asked his father by signs.
Mary stayed with me about three months, then returned home.
Jehovah magnified his mercy to me at my son's birth.
Barren and well along in years, I conceived, then hid myself five months until Jehovah took away my reproach.
When Mary greeted me, I was filled with holy spirit, my unborn child leaped, and I blessed the mother of my Lord.
Against the relatives' wish to name him Zechariah, I said he would be called John.
From Aaron's line and married to a priest of Abijah's division, I bore the child Gabriel named John.
I had John the Baptizer beheaded.
I hoped to see Jesus perform some sign.
I married Herodias, my brother's wife.
I put John in prison.
I questioned Jesus at length, but he gave me no answer.
I sent Jesus back to Pilate.
I was district ruler of Galilee.
Pilate sent Jesus to me.
Chief priests and scribes stood accusing Jesus before me.
Herodias's daughter danced before me and my guests.
I clothed Jesus with a bright garment.
I heard reports about Jesus and was perplexed.
I kept seeking to see Jesus.
I said John I beheaded, so who is this about whom I hear such things?
I swore to give Herodias's daughter whatever she asked.
I was in Jerusalem in those days when Pilate sent Jesus to me.
John reproved me concerning Herodias.
John said it was not lawful for me to have my brother's wife.
On my birthday I held a banquet.
Pilate and I became friends with each other that very day.
Though grieved, I commanded that John be beheaded because of my oaths and the guests.
With my soldiers I treated Jesus with contempt and mocked him.
Before that day Pilate and I had been at enmity with each other.
Herodias was the wife of my brother Philip.
I also faced reproof over all the wicked things I had done.
I feared John, knowing he was a righteous and holy man.
I feared the crowd because they held John as a prophet.
I kept John safe.
I told Herodias's daughter to ask me for up to half my kingdom.
My leading men, military commanders, and the most prominent men of Galilee were at my birthday banquet.
I told my servants that Jesus was John the Baptizer raised from the dead.
On top of those things, I locked John up in prison.
Pharisees warned Jesus that I wanted to kill him.
Herodias' daughter asked me for John's head on a platter.
Some said Jesus was John raised up—the John I had beheaded.
When I listened to John, I was much perplexed, yet I heard him gladly.
When Pilate learned Jesus was under my jurisdiction, he sent him to me.
After beheading John, I heard the reports about Jesus and was perplexed, saying John I beheaded—who is this?
Bound by birthday oaths before Galilee's prominent men, I handed John's head to Herodias's daughter on a platter.
I protected John and heard him gladly, then killed him to keep an oath before dinner guests.
Jesus called me a fox when told I wanted him killed, and I later met him when Pilate sent him to me.
Jesus told them to go say to me, that fox, that he was casting out demons and performing cures.
I was king of Judea when Jesus was born.
Astrologers from eastern parts came to me in Jerusalem.
I asked the chief priests and scribes where the Christ was to be born.
I was deeply disturbed when I heard of one born king of the Jews.
I sent the astrologers to Bethlehem.
I ordered the killing of the boys in Bethlehem.
Joseph fled to Egypt because of me.
All Jerusalem was stirred with me at the astrologers' report.
I assembled the chief priests and scribes of the people.
They told me the Christ was to be born in Bethlehem of Judea.
I learned the time of the star's appearing from the astrologers.
I summoned the astrologers secretly.
I told them to go search carefully for the young child.
I said when you find him, report back to me so I may also go and do him homage.
The astrologers were given divine warning not to return to me.
When I saw I had been outwitted by the astrologers, I flew into a rage.
I targeted boys two years of age and under.
My massacre reached Bethlehem and all its districts.
An angel told Joseph to stay in Egypt until I died.
Micah's words about Bethlehem were cited to me as the place of birth.
I calculated the boys' ages from the time I learned from the astrologers.
Jeremiah's cry about Rachel weeping was tied to what I did in that region.
After I died, an angel told Joseph in Egypt that those seeking the child's life were dead.
Archelaus began ruling Judea in place of me his father.
Zechariah's priestly service is dated to my days as king of Judea.
King when astrologers sought one born king of the Jews, I probed Scripture experts, then claimed that I too wanted to do him homage.
Outwitted when the astrologers never returned, I slaughtered Bethlehem's boys two and under by the star's timing.
My hunt drove the child to Egypt until my death, after which Archelaus ruled in my place.
Luke dates John's parents to my reign; Matthew records I tried to destroy the child born in my days.
I was married to Herod.
John said it was not lawful for Herod to have me.
I wanted John put to death.
My daughter asked for John's head because of me.
John's head was brought to me on a platter.
I had been the wife of Philip, Herod's brother.
I held a grudge against John.
I was unable to put John to death at first.
On Herod's birthday my daughter danced.
Herod swore an oath to my daughter.
My daughter came in and asked me what she should request.
I said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
My daughter brought the head and gave it to me.
Herod locked John up on my account.
Luke says Herod was reproved concerning me, his brother's wife.
Herod feared killing John even while I wanted him dead.
I used Herod's birthday oath and my daughter's dance to finish what I could not do alone.
After becoming Herod's wife while his brother Philip was alive, I became the subject of John's reproof.
Nursing a grudge I could not satisfy, I coached my dancing daughter to demand John's head.
Herod's birthday oath delivered to me John the Baptizer's head on a platter.
I was a synagogue ruler.
I fell at Jesus' feet.
I begged Jesus to come to my house.
My only daughter was about 12 years old.
Jesus raised my daughter from the dead.
Jesus told me not to fear, only to exercise faith.
My little daughter was extremely ill.
I asked Jesus to put his hands on her so she would get well and live.
While Jesus was going with me, a woman touched his garment.
Messengers said my daughter had died.
They asked why I bother the Teacher further.
At my house people were weeping and wailing loudly.
Jesus said my child had not died but was sleeping.
Jesus took me and the child's mother inside with him.
After my daughter rose, Jesus ordered that she be given something to eat.
Matthew calls me a ruler who came and did obeisance to Jesus.
I told Jesus my daughter had just died, yet asked him to come and lay his hand on her.
Jesus ordered us strictly not to let anyone know what had happened.
My daughter got up at once and began walking.
Jesus allowed no one to accompany him to my house except Peter, James, and John.
Those present began to laugh at Jesus when he said my daughter was sleeping.
As synagogue ruler I fell before Jesus for my only 12-year-old daughter, then heard she had died on the way.
Told only to exercise faith, I entered with Peter, James, John, and my wife while mourners laughed.
After Jesus took her hand and she rose, we were told to feed her and keep silent.
I was a brother of Jesus.
People named me among Jesus' brothers with Joseph, Simon, and Judas.
Jesus appeared to me after his resurrection.
Peter said to report his escape to me and the brothers.
I spoke with decisive counsel at the Jerusalem meeting about circumcision.
Paul came to see me in Jerusalem with the older men.
I lived at Nazareth as one of Jesus' household brothers.
After Jesus' ascension I was in an upper room with the apostles, Mary, and my brothers.
At the gathering of the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, I said, “Men, brothers, hear me.”
I reviewed how God turned his attention to the nations.
I cited the Prophets as agreeing that God would turn his attention to the nations.
I judged that they should not trouble people from the nations who are turning to God.
I listed abstaining from things polluted by idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood.
Cephas, John, and I were regarded as pillars and gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.
Jude called himself a brother of mine.
Paul said he saw none of the other apostles except me, the brother of the Lord.
Early on, I and Jesus' other brothers were not exercising faith in him.
Jesus' sisters were mentioned along with us brothers.
Men from me arrived in Antioch, and Cephas withdrew from eating with people of the nations.
Paul went up to Jerusalem to the apostles and older men about the circumcision issue before I gave judgment.
Believers later told Paul that thousands of Jews who had believed were zealous for the Law, in the setting of his visit to me.
I proposed writing the nations with those four necessary things.
Before the Festival of Tabernacles, I and my brothers urged Jesus to go into Judea.
Once listed among unbelieving brothers at Nazareth, I later received a resurrection appearance and led counsel in Jerusalem.
Called the brother of the Lord by Paul, I stood as a pillar with Cephas and John and defined the decree for believing people of the nations.
Jude introduced himself as my brother, tying his letter to my household name.
I was one of the twelve apostles.
I was the son of Alphaeus.
Jesus chose me among the twelve.
I was still named among the apostles in an upper room after Jesus' ascension.
The Gospel accounts name me among the twelve apostles.
I remained in Jerusalem with the apostles after Jesus was taken up.
In Matthew's list I appear after Matthew the tax collector.
In Acts I was listed with the other surviving apostles in Jerusalem.
I shared my name with the son of Zebedee, but my father was Alphaeus.
Though little is recorded of my deeds, I was numbered with the twelve and remained among them after the ascension.
In the lists of apostles I was distinguished as the son of Alphaeus.
Chosen among the twelve as the son of Alphaeus, I stayed with the apostles in Jerusalem after Jesus was taken up.
Herod the king killed me with the sword.
I was the son of Zebedee.
I left my father Zebedee in a boat and followed Jesus.
I was one of the twelve apostles.
Jesus called me while I was a fisherman.
Jesus surnamed my brother and me Boanerges, Sons of Thunder.
John the apostle was my brother.
Hired men remained with my father when we left.
I was mending nets with John when Jesus called us.
Jesus asked if we could drink the cup he was drinking.
Jesus took me with Peter and John farther into Gethsemane.
Jesus took me with Peter and John to raise Jairus's daughter.
My brother and I asked if we should call fire from heaven on a Samaritan village.
My brother and I asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in his glory.
Simon and I were partners in the fishing work.
The other ten became indignant at us.
When Jesus asked if we could drink the cup he was drinking, my brother and I said we were able.
I was named with John among those present at the catch of fish after Jesus' resurrection.
In the apostle lists I was paired with my brother John.
Jesus turned and rebuked us for asking to call down fire.
Jesus said the seats at his right and left were not his to give when I asked with my brother.
Jesus said we would drink his cup.
Jesus took me with Peter and John up into a lofty mountain where he was transfigured.
My mother came with us and requested the seats at Jesus' right and left.
On the Mount of Olives I asked privately with Peter, John, and Andrew about the sign.
I shared my name with the son of Alphaeus, but my father was Zebedee.
I was the first of the Twelve Scripture names as killed for the faith.
After seeking fire on Samaritans and seats in glory, I drank the cup when Herod killed me with the sword.
Called from Zebedee's boat with John, nicknamed Sons of Thunder, I later fell by Herod's sword.
A voice from heaven called me God's Son at my baptism.
After I was raised, I appeared to my disciples.
Fishermen were among my first disciples.
I was called God's Anointed One.
I was called the Son of man.
I ascended to heaven in a cloud.
I called 12 men as my apostles.
I calmed a windstorm on the sea.
I cast out demons.
I entered Jerusalem riding on a donkey.
I fasted 40 days in the wilderness.
I fed about 5,000 men with five loaves and two fish.
I gave my disciples a model prayer.
I grew up in Nazareth.
I healed many who were sick.
I predicted that I would be killed and raised up.
I said, “I am the way and the truth and the life.”
I said I was not sent forth to any but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
I said "Lazarus, come out!", and he rose from the dead and came out of the tomb.
I said love Jehovah your God and love your neighbor.
I said, “Come to me, all you who are toiling.”
I said, “It has been accomplished!” before I died.
I taught crowds on a mountain in Galilee.
I taught in synagogues.
I told Thomas to see my hands and my side.
I told my disciples to love one another.
I turned water into wine at Cana.
I walked on the sea.
I was born in Bethlehem.
I was executed on a torture stake.
I was raised up on the third day.
I washed my disciples' feet.
John baptized me in the Jordan.
Joseph of Arimathea placed me in his new tomb.
Judas Iscariot betrayed me.
Mary Magdalene saw me after I was raised.
My mother was Mary.
Peter, James, and John were among those closest to me.
Pilate handed me over to be impaled.
Soldiers mocked me as King of the Jews.
The Devil tempted me in the wilderness.
A soldier pierced my side with a spear.
A woman was healed when she touched my outer garment.
After my resurrection I asked Peter three times if he loved me.
Astrologers from the east came looking for me as a young child.
At 12 years of age I stayed behind in the temple among the teachers.
At one time even my brothers did not exercise faith in me.
Barabbas was released instead of me.
By the Sea of Galilee I served my disciples a breakfast of fish.
Capernaum became a base for my preaching.
Darkness covered the land for three hours while I was on the stake.
I asked a Samaritan woman for a drink at Jacob's fountain.
I called Matthew away from the tax office.
I cast a legion of demons into a herd of swine.
I commissioned my disciples to make disciples of people of all the nations.
I cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
I drove sellers and money changers out of the temple.
I fed about 4,000 men with seven loaves.
I forgave a paralyzed man's sins before I healed him.
I found no fruit on a fig tree and cursed it.
I healed Peter's mother-in-law of a fever.
I healed an army officer's servant from a distance.
I healed ten men with leprosy.
I instituted a meal for my disciples to keep in remembrance of me.
I invited tax collectors and sinners to eat with me.
I opened the eyes of a man born blind.
I prayed in a garden called Gethsemane.
I predicted that Peter would deny me three times.
I predicted that the temple stones would be thrown down.
I raised Jairus's daughter.
I raised a widow's only son at Nain.
I said, “I am the bread of life.”
I said, “I am the good shepherd.”
I said, “I am the light of the world.”
I said, “I am the resurrection and the life.”
I said, “I am the true vine.”
I said I would be with them all the days until the conclusion of the system of things.
I said a city cannot be hid when located on a mountain.
I said a tree is known by its fruit.
I said all authority has been given me in heaven and on the earth.
I said build your house on rock, not on sand.
I said continue to love your enemies and to pray for those persecuting you.
I said do to others as you want them to do to you.
I said enter through the narrow gate.
I said greater love has no one than this, that someone surrender his life for his friends.
I said in the world you will have tribulation, but take courage.
I said keep on seeking first the Kingdom.
I said keep on the watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
I said let the dead bury their dead.
I said let your light shine before men.
I said my sheep listen to my voice.
I said my yoke is kindly and my load is light.
I said no one comes to the Father except through me.
I said render Caesar's things to Caesar, but God's things to God.
I said stop judging that you may not be judged.
I said stop storing up treasures on the earth.
I said the Sabbath came into existence for man's sake.
I said the Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath.
I said the greatest among you must be your minister.
I said the truth will set you free.
I said this good news of the Kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth.
I said whatever you ask the Father in my name he will give you.
I said, “Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in their midst.”
I said whoever exalts himself will be humbled.
I said why do you look at the straw in your brother's eye?
I said you cannot slave for God and for Riches.
I said you heard that it was said, 'Eye for eye,' but I say do not resist the wicked one.
I sent out 70 disciples ahead of me.
I slept in a boat while a windstorm rose.
I told Nicodemus that a man must be born again.
I told Zacchaeus to come down so I could stay at his house.
I told a parable about a Pharisee and a tax collector praying in the temple.
I told a parable about a Samaritan who showed mercy to a wounded man.
I told a parable about a father who ran to welcome his lost son.
I told a parable about a marriage feast for a king's son.
I told a parable about a persistent widow and an unrighteous judge.
I told a parable about a rich man and Lazarus the beggar.
I told a parable about a sower who scattered seed on different kinds of soil.
I told a parable about an unrighteous steward.
I told a parable about murderous cultivators of a vineyard.
I told a parable about talents entrusted to slaves.
I told a parable about ten virgins who took their lamps to meet the bridegroom.
I told a parable about two sons, one who said he would go and did not.
I told a parable about wheat and weeds sown in a field.
I told a parable about workers hired at different hours for a denarius.
I told a rich young man to sell his belongings and give to the poor.
I took little children into my arms and blessed them.
I was about 30 years old when I began my work.
I was taken to Egypt when Herod sought to destroy me.
I was transfigured before Peter, James, and John.
I wept at Lazarus's memorial tomb.
I wept over Jerusalem.
Moses and Elijah appeared with me on a mountain.
My hometown tried to throw me off a precipice.
Near Jericho I restored Bartimaeus's sight.
Religious leaders said I cast out demons by Beelzebub.
Simon of Cyrene was compelled to carry my torture stake.
Soldiers cast lots for my outer garment.
About 2,000 swine rushed into the sea after I cast out Legion.
After I was raised I appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
After I was raised I appeared to more than 500 brothers at one time.
After rising I breathed holy spirit on my disciples.
After supper I sang praises with my apostles before going to the Mount of Olives.
An army officer watching me die declared that I was God's Son.
Crowds tried to seize me to make me king after I fed them.
From the Mount of Olives I was taken up while my disciples looked on.
Herod Antipas questioned me at length, but I gave him no answer.
I appeared to my disciples by the sea while they were fishing after my resurrection.
I asked my disciples, “Who are men saying the Son of man is?”
I called Lazarus out of the memorial tomb with a loud voice.
I named Simon Peter and later called him a stumbling block when he opposed my path to death.
I compared the Kingdom to a mustard grain that becomes a tree where birds find lodging.
I compared the Kingdom to yeast that a woman took and hid in three large measures of flour.
